title: Verbs of Change: How Music Became Popular

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the verbs of change *ponerse*, *volverse*, *hacerse* and *quedarse* from B1 Unit 25. *Ponerse* + adjective is a mood or state that can pass; *volverse* + adjective is a deeper change; *hacerse* + noun is a change you reach with time or effort; *quedarse* is a result; and *convertirse en* is a bigger change. The stories of merengue and bachata are stories of change.

sections.title: Which verb of change?
rows: Los bailarines se ponen contentos al oír un merengue.
La bachata se volvió popular en muchos países.
Con los años, el merengue se hizo música nacional.
Cuando acabó la canción, la sala se quedó en silencio.

items.spanish: Algunos bailarines se ponen tristes al oír una bachata de amargue.
items.english: Some dancers become sad when they hear a bachata of heartbreak.

items.spanish: Después de 1990, la bachata se volvió popular en muchos países.
items.english: After 1990, bachata became popular in many countries.

items.spanish: Con los años, el merengue se convirtió en un símbolo nacional.
items.english: Over the years, merengue became a national symbol.

items.spanish: Al terminar el concierto, el público se quedó sin voz.
items.english: When the concert ended, the audience was left without a voice.

sections.content: Choose the verb by the kind of change: *ponerse* and *quedarse* for a state that can pass or a result, *volverse* for a deeper change, *hacerse* and *convertirse en* + noun for a change over time. These verbs are reflexive, so they always have *se*.
